data.name: Reformers
data.detailed_description:
Introduction

Reformers is a retro role-playing game, the story line is based on Picasso's "Guernica" to unfold the aerial world view. The game is based on traditional turn-based combat, and the player character has no fixed career setting, instead, it can fight with the monster, and the clever collocation can also get unexpected effects, so that the player can choose freely.

In the game, you will become a REFORMER, who is going to save the world. By using your special skill, the Soul Alliance, you will beat different enemies, prevent the dark cabal’s evil, collect souls of monsters or even take them as servants. At last, don’t forget to enhance the Power of Crystals. The future of reformers is in danger, and your great rescue is on the way.

The Beginning of the Story — Reformers with the power to fuse with monsters!

In this war-torn era, on a continent overrun by monsters, the fragmented imperial powers see the nobles of Prokade Castle and the Stiake Kingdom embroiled in a series of conflicts over territory and influence. To secure victory, the aristocracy requires soldiers of exceptional prowess on the battlefield. These soldiers often possess the unique ability to 'fight in alliance' with monsters, and have come to be known as 'Reformers'. With the involvement of these Reformers, the nature of warfare has shifted from human-versus-human conflicts to battles where humans and monsters fight side-by-side against other humans, creating an overwhelming, one-sided advantage in the theater of war.

Follow the legend and lift the veil on the past!

King of Prokade Castle realized that the wars among the nobles had begun to threaten his own authority. He dispatched three of the kingdom's most powerful knights - Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo di Lodovico, and Raphael Sanzio. These three knights led massive armies to quell the conflicts.

Da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Raphael were all formidable Reformers within the kingdom. However, only da Vinci was the inheritor of 'The Last Supper', possessing the ultimate power to command legions of monsters. For a time, the combined forces of Prokade Castle's human troops and monster legions, led by da Vinci, swept across the continent, meeting little resistance. The King and nobles of the Stiake Kingdom ultimately surrendered and swore allegiance to the King of Prokade Castle. With the war concluded, the three knights of Prokade Castle returned home in triumph.

The calm before the storm, and the battle is on the verge of breaking out!

At the victory banquet, the king conferred honors upon da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Raphael. Yet even then, misgivings began to stir within him. The king and his nobles had all witnessed da Vinci's unimaginable power, which the king now saw as a potential threat to his rule. The nobles, whispering poisonous counsel at his side, urged the king to find a way to eliminate da Vinci and the others.

As expected, within a few years after the conflict was quelled, Michelangelo was framed for colluding with the Stiake Kingdom and exiled. Raphael was demoted on trumped-up charges. Only da Vinci's whereabouts remained unknown. Subsequently, the king issued orders for the widespread purge of other Reformers who possessed the ability to ally with monsters. In short order, anyone with Reformer heritage faced systematic eradication.

With this perceived threat removed, the ambitions of the nobility began to surge once more. A new war became inevitable, and Prokade Castle was once again plunged into a bloody conflict.

And thus our story begins... on the distant Halesia Island, far beyond the borders of Prokade Castle.

Notes

  • Press F11 to switch between full-screen and windowed mode.

  • Impressionism, Fauvism, and Surrealism are server names (servers were permanently shut down in April 2025).

  • Art: TXBD, Programming: GXM, Completed independently by two individuals.

reviews.review:
Reformers, created and published by RMking, is a retro-styled role-playing game that embraces the design philosophy of classic 1990s Japanese RPGs while layering in a distinctive creature-alliance system that gives it its own identity. From the outset, it feels like a deliberate homage to an earlier era of gaming—an era defined by pixel art sprites, turn-based encounters, overworld exploration, and character growth rooted in gradual progression rather than cinematic spectacle. Rather than attempting to modernize every aspect of its design, Reformers leans confidently into nostalgia, building an experience that prioritizes mechanics, party-building, and steady exploration.

At the heart of the game lies the soul alliance mechanic, which allows the protagonist to forge contracts with the spirits of defeated enemies. This system introduces a compelling strategic twist: instead of relying solely on a fixed cast of party members, players can recruit and deploy enemy souls as combat allies. Each soul brings its own abilities, elemental affinities, and tactical strengths, encouraging experimentation and thoughtful team composition. Deciding which souls to bring into battle becomes an important part of the gameplay loop, especially as encounters grow more challenging. The mechanic blends traditional RPG party management with a creature-collection influence, giving combat a layer of flexibility beyond standard character leveling.

Combat adheres to classic turn-based principles. Encounters unfold in structured rounds where players select commands from menus, balancing offensive attacks, defensive maneuvers, and special abilities. The pacing is methodical, rewarding careful planning rather than rapid input. Enemy patterns, elemental weaknesses, and status effects all factor into tactical decisions. While the system may not introduce highly complex mechanics by modern RPG standards, it succeeds in delivering satisfying strategic depth through synergy between the protagonist and allied souls. As players progress, new skills and stronger souls expand combat possibilities, reinforcing the sense of growth central to traditional RPGs.

Exploration follows a familiar structure that will resonate with fans of classic console role-playing games. Players travel across interconnected maps, visit towns populated with NPCs, and delve into dungeons filled with enemies and hidden treasures. The world design encourages steady progression, with new areas unlocking as story events unfold. NPC dialogue provides narrative context and occasional side objectives, enriching the setting without overwhelming players with exposition. The story itself centers on themes of transformation and destiny, positioning the protagonist as a pivotal figure in a changing world. While the narrative presentation is modest and dialogue-driven, it aligns with the game’s nostalgic aesthetic and pacing.

Visually, Reformers embraces pixel art with deliberate simplicity. Character sprites, environmental tilesets, and battle animations evoke the 16-bit era, favoring clarity and charm over graphical complexity. The art style reinforces the retro atmosphere, making the game feel like a rediscovered classic rather than a modern reinterpretation. Animation work remains functional and expressive enough to convey personality and action without overcomplicating the visual presentation. Complementing the visuals is a soundtrack that supports exploration and battle with melodies reminiscent of older RPG sound design, further grounding the experience in its chosen era.

The pacing of Reformers is steady and intentionally traditional. Progression unfolds gradually through exploration, combat, and story advancement rather than rapid-fire set pieces. Players who appreciate slow-burn development and incremental character growth will likely find the rhythm satisfying. However, those accustomed to modern RPG conveniences—such as streamlined quest tracking, extensive tutorials, or cinematic storytelling—may find the experience more understated. The game’s commitment to classic structure means it avoids excessive hand-holding, instead trusting players to learn systems organically.

Ultimately, Reformers stands as a focused and heartfelt homage to retro role-playing design. Its soul alliance system gives it a distinctive hook, while its combat and exploration systems faithfully recreate the feeling of classic turn-based adventures. Though it may not reinvent the genre or introduce groundbreaking mechanics, it succeeds in delivering a cohesive and enjoyable experience rooted in nostalgia and strategic party-building. For players who cherish pixel art RPGs and methodical combat systems, Reformers offers a compact yet rewarding journey that honors the traditions of its inspiration while adding its own unique flavor.

Rating: 7/10
